elements.content: Grammar focus: Participle Clauses for Background Information.

Core Rule: Participle clauses replace full subordinate clauses when both clauses share the same subject: Present Participle (-ing) for simultaneous action/cause, Past Participle (-ed) for passive condition, Perfect Participle (Having + V3) for prior completed action.

Present Participle — Verb-ing + Complement...: Examining the demographic data , researchers noted an urban migration shift.
Past Participle — Past Participle + Complement...: Drafted in haste , the legislation contained several regulatory loopholes.
Perfect Participle — Having + Past Participle...: Having secured shareholder approval , the executive board launched the buyout.
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Which sentence correctly uses a perfect participle clause?
options: Having completed the inspection, the engineer signed the certification.
Having completed the inspection, the certificate was signed by the engineer.

elements.content: 2. When can a participle clause be used to replace a full clause?
options: When both clauses share the same logical subject

elements.content: Read and listen: three examples in context.

Built in 1850, the bridge is still used.
